title: Professions, Articles & Clear Sentences
subtitle: B1 practice with profession vocabulary, sentence construction and articles.
lessonNotes: Review profession vocabulary and use it in clear sentences.
Review a, an, the and no article before the next lesson.
Practise listening for job words, skills and responsibilities.

grammar.title: A and an
grammar.rule: Use a or an for one singular profession.

grammar.title: The
grammar.rule: Use the for a specific person or job that is already clear.

grammar.title: No article
grammar.rule: Use no article for professions in general in the plural.

grammar.title: Clear sentences
grammar.rule: Use a subject, a correct verb and useful information about duties or place.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who designs or repairs systems
a person who works with medicine
a person who writes news stories
a person who repairs water pipes
a person who cares for teeth
a person who takes professional photographs
a person who creates computer programs

practice.q: In a careers-fair profile, complete: ‘Mila is ___ architect.’
practice.explanation: Use an because architect starts with a vowel sound.

opt: An chef works in a kitchen.
A chef works in a kitchen.
practice.a: A chef works in a kitchen.

reading.title: A Day at the Careers Fair
reading.text: Students speak to professionals, learn what different jobs involve and write sentences about work they find interesting.

listening.title: You’re Hired: Episode 03 (B1)
listening.instructions: Watch the interview-preparation episode. Listen first for the main purpose, then note job words, skills and responsibilities.
listening.script: Use the linked activity's video and exercises before answering the strategy questions.

questions.q: During a second watch, a learner writes down skills and responsibilities. Is this a useful strategy?

writing: Write 90–120 words about a profession you find interesting. Use a, an, the and no article correctly.
Write five clear sentences about five different professions.
Write a short careers-fair dialogue with questions and answers about work.

quiz.q: In a staff profile, complete: ‘She is ___ engineer.’
quiz.explanation: Use an before engineer because it starts with a vowel sound.

quiz.q: In a restaurant review, complete: ‘He is ___ chef.’
quiz.explanation: Use a before chef because it starts with a consonant sound.

quiz.q: A careers guide says: ‘___ pharmacists work with medicine.’
quiz.explanation: No article is needed for pharmacists in general.

quiz.q: A patient says: ‘___ dentist at this clinic is friendly.’
quiz.explanation: Use the because this refers to one specific dentist.

quiz.q: A restaurant is writing a staff introduction. Select the best sentence.
opt: An chef works in a kitchen.
A chef works in a kitchen.
quiz.a: A chef works in a kitchen.
quiz.explanation: A singular profession needs an article, and chef takes a.
Use an before architect because it starts with a vowel sound.

quiz.q: A school poster makes a general statement. Select the natural version.
quiz.explanation: No article is used for engineers in general.

quiz.q: A menu says, ‘The chef recommends the soup.’ Why is the chef specific?
quiz.explanation: Use the when the situation makes one particular chef clear.

quiz.q: A school notice says: ‘My mother is ___.’
quiz.explanation: University begins with a /j/ sound, so it takes a.

quiz.q: A pharmacy website needs one clear sentence. Select it.
quiz.explanation: The sentence uses an article, correct word order and the singular verb helps.

opt: say a long word in parts
quiz.a: say a long word in parts
